claim: CD4+ T cells use T cell receptor (TCR)–CD3 complexes and CD4 to respond to peptide antigens within MHCII molecules (pMHCII).
source: CD4+ T cells use T cell receptor (TCR)–CD3 complexes, and CD4, to respond to peptide antigens within MHCII molecules (pMHCII).
evidence: This is a foundational statement about CD4+ T cell biology that is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Purifying selection has shaped motifs in the extracellular, transmembrane, and intracellular domains of eutherian CD4 that enhance pMHCII responses through approximately 435 million years of evolution in jawed vertebrates.
source: through ~435 million years of evolution in jawed vertebrates, purifying selection has shaped motifs in the extracellular, transmembrane, and intracellular domains of eutherian CD4 that enhance pMHCII responses
evidence: The manuscript presents evolutionary analyses showing purifying selection on specific CD4 motifs across vertebrate evolution.

claim: Motifs in eutherian CD4 that enhance pMHCII responses covary with residues in an intracellular motif that inhibits responses.
source: purifying selection has shaped motifs in the extracellular, transmembrane, and intracellular domains of eutherian CD4 that enhance pMHCII responses, and covary with residues in an intracellular motif that inhibits responses.
evidence: The manuscript presents covariation analysis and functional data showing that enhancing and inhibitory motifs covary.

claim: CD4 interactions with the Src kinase Lck are viewed as key to pMHCII responses.
source: while CD4 interactions with the Src kinase, Lck, are viewed as key to pMHCII responses
evidence: This represents the established paradigm in the field, cited as existing knowledge.

claim: CD4–Lck interactions derive their importance from the counterbalancing activity of an inhibitory motif and motifs that direct CD4–Lck pairs to specific membrane compartments.
source: our data indicate that CD4–Lck interactions derive their importance from the counterbalancing activity of the inhibitory motif, as well as motifs that direct CD4–Lck pairs to specific membrane compartments.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on functional assays and biochemical analyses.

claim: The immunological 'Big Bang' that gave rise to RAG-based antigen receptor gene rearrangement in jawed vertebrates produced an adaptive immune system in which each naive B and T cell expresses a clonotypic receptor with unique antigen specificity.
source: The immunological 'Big Bang' that gave rise to RAG-based antigen receptor gene rearrangement in jawed vertebrates produced an adaptive immune system in which each naive B and T cell expresses a clonotypic B or T cell receptor (BCR or TCR) with unique antigen specificity (Bernstein et al., 1996; Flajnik, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TCRs that interact weakly with self-pMHCII direct positive selection toward the CD4+ lineage.
source: TCRs that interact weakly with self-pMHCII direct positive selection toward the CD4+ lineage
evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell development, supported by citation.

claim: TCRs that strongly recognize self-pMHCII induce apoptosis to establish central tolerance by removing autoreactive TCR clonotypes from the repertoire by negative selection.
source: while those that strongly recognize self-pMHCII induce apoptosis to establish central tolerance by removing autoreactive TCR clonotypes from the repertoire by negative selection.
evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell development.

claim: The TCR is the receptor module that deciphers information encoded within the composite pMHCII surface and relays the information to the immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs) of three associated signaling modules.
source: The TCR is the receptor module. It deciphers information encoded within the composite pMHCII surface and relays the information to the immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs) of three associated signaling modules (CD3γε, CD3δε, and CD3ζζ) (Chen et al., 2022; Gil et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CD4 binds MHCII on the outside of the CD4+ T cell and interacts with the Src kinase Lck via an intracellular CQC clasp motif.
source: It binds MHCII on the outside of the CD4+ T cell and interacts with the Src kinase, Lck, via an intracellular CQC clasp motif (Kim et al., 2003; Turner et al., 1990).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: According to the TCR signaling paradigm, CD4 recruits Lck to phosphorylate the ITAMs of TCR–CD3 complexes when both TCR–CD3 and CD4 coincidently engage pMHCII.
source: According to the TCR signaling paradigm, CD4 recruits Lck to phosphorylate the ITAMs of TCR–CD3 complexes when both TCR–CD3 and CD4 coincidently engage pMHCII (Rudd, 2021).
evidence: This describes the established paradigm, supported by citation.

claim: CD4's extracellular domain can increase TCR dwell time on pMHCII and position its intracellular domain in a defined relationship with the TCR–CD3 complex through coordinated rather than coincident interactions.
source: CD4's extracellular domain (ECD) can increase TCR dwell time on pMHCII and position its intracellular domain (ICD) in a defined relationship with the TCR–CD3 complex through coordinated rather than coincident interactions (Glassman et al., 2016; Glassman et al., 2018; Guy and Vignali, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CD4 molecules that are not associated with Lck have been proposed to compete with those that are to limit the number of TCR–CD3 complexes phosphorylated by Lck.
source: Furthermore, CD4 molecules that are not associated with Lck have been proposed to compete with those that are to limit the number of TCR–CD3 complexes phosphorylated by Lck, thus setting a threshold for the duration of TCR–pMHCII interactions required to initiate signaling (Stepanek et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a proposed model from prior work, supported by citation.

claim: CD4 molecules associated with Lck play a vital role in pMHCII restriction by sequestering Lck away from TCR–CD3 to prevent off-target signaling by TCR interactions with non-pMHCII molecules.
source: In addition, CD4 molecules that are associated with Lck are reported to play a vital role in pMHCII restriction by sequestering Lck away from TCR–CD3 to prevent off-target signaling by TCR interactions with non-pMHCII molecules (Van Laethem et al., 2013).
evidence: This is reported in prior work, supported by citation.

claim: The analyzed CD4 sequences represent approximately 435 million years of evolution.
source: We performed multiple analyses of available vertebrate CD4 ortholog sequences (n = 99 distinct sequences), representing ~435 million years of evolution
evidence: This is based on the evolutionary analysis performed in the study.

claim: Analysis of sequence conservation showed particular conservation in the intracellular domain (ICD) of CD4.
source: Analysis of sequence conservation between the full set of extant CD4 molecules, or mammalian CD4 molecules only, showed particular conservation in the ICD (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Of the 17 codons under diversifying selection in CD4, 16 (94.1%) are distributed across the CD4 ectodomain while only one is found in the TMD.
source: Of the 17 codons under diversifying selection, 16 (94.1%) are distributed across the CD4 ectodomain while only one is found in the TMD.
evidence: This is based on the dN:dS ratio analysis performed in the study.

claim: 45.5% of TMD codons (10 of 22) and 45% (18 of 40) within the ICD are under purifying selection.
source: In contrast, 45.5% of TMD codons (10 of 22) and 45% (18 of 40) within the ICD are under purifying selection.
evidence: This is based on the dN:dS ratio analysis performed in the study.

claim: The predicted most recent common ancestor of all amniotes contains a PLXF motif (mouse 228–231) in the D3 domain that is maintained in mammals.
source: The predicted most recent common ancestor of all amniotes contains a PLXF motif (mouse 228–231) in the D3 domain that is maintained in mammals (Figure 1A, node 1).
evidence: This is based on phylogenetic reconstruction shown in Figure 1A.

claim: P281 is not found in the predicted amniote most recent common ancestor but is in the mammalian most recent common ancestor and extant mammals.
source: P281 is not found in the predicted amniote most recent common ancestor but is in the mammalian most recent common ancestor, and extant mammals, suggesting that it arose after mammals diverged from reptiles.
evidence: This is based on phylogenetic reconstruction and inference about evolutionary timing.

claim: P228, L229, F231, and P281 have small dN:dS values that are primarily driven by low dN rates, indicating that changing these residues likely affects fitness.
source: Importantly, P228, L229, F231, and P281 have small dN:dS values that are primarily driven by low dN rates, indicating that changing these residues likely affects fitness.
evidence: This is based on the dN:dS analysis and represents an inference about fitness effects.

claim: The predicted most recent common ancestor of all amniotes contains a GG patch (G402 and G403) in its TMD that is lost in nonavian reptiles but present in extant birds.
source: For example, the predicted most recent common ancestor of all amniotes (node 1) contains a GG patch (G402 and G403) in its TMD that is lost in nonavian reptiles but present in extant birds (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on phylogenetic reconstruction shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the predicted eutherian most recent common ancestor, the GG patch expanded into a highly conserved GGXXG motif that is present in the majority of eutherian CD4 proteins.
source: In the predicted eutherian most recent common ancestor (node 4), the GG patch expanded into a highly conserved GGXXG motif that is present in the majority of eutherian CD4 proteins (see logo plot) including mouse and human.
evidence: This is based on phylogenetic reconstruction and logo plot analysis.

claim: G402 and G403 were found to be under purifying selection using both the full and mammal-only dataset, while G406 was only identified in the full dataset.
source: Importantly, G402 and G403 were found to be under purifying selection using both the full and mammal-only dataset, while G406 was only identified in the full dataset (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on the dN:dS analysis shown in the figures.

claim: A CV+C motif is highly conserved in eutherian CD4 molecules but not present in the predicted mammalian most recent common ancestor or marsupials.
source: Our approach also identified a CV +C motif ('+' represents a basic residue) that is highly conserved in eutherian CD4 molecules but not present in the predicted mammalian most recent common ancestor or marsupials (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on phylogenetic reconstruction shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Palmitoylation of cysteines in the CV+C motif is reported to influence membrane raft localization.
source: Palmitoylation of these cysteines is reported to influence membrane raft localization, although this is controversial as association with Lck may also localize CD4 to membrane rafts (Crise and Rose, 1992; Fragoso et al., 2003; Ladygina et al., 2011).
evidence: This is reported in prior work, supported by citations, though noted as controversial.

claim: The combination of the CV+C and the GGXXG/S motifs are unique to extant eutherians and co-arose during evolution.
source: Our analyses suggest that the combination of the CV +C and the GGXXG/S motifs are unique to extant eutherians, co-arose during evolution, and may work together to regulate CD4 membrane localization.
evidence: This is based on the evolutionary analysis and represents an inference about their function.

claim: A poly-basic RHRRR motif in the juxtamembrane region of the ICD was previously reported to impact human CD4 localization to membrane rafts.
source: A poly-basic RHRRR motif in the juxtamembrane region of the ICD was also previously reported to impact human CD4 localization to membrane rafts (Popik and Alce, 2004).
evidence: This is reported in prior work, supported by citation.

claim: Comparative analyses suggest a core HXXR motif (mouse 423–426) with H423 and R426 under purifying selection in the full dataset, and R426 under purifying selection in the mammal-only dataset.
source: Our comparative analyses suggest a core HXXR motif (mouse 423–426) with H423 and R426 under purifying selection in the full dataset, and R426 under purifying selection in the mammal-only dataset (Figure 1A, B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on the evolutionary analysis shown in the figures.

claim: The ICD of human CD4 contains a helix-turn structure, the sequence of which is highly conserved in mammalian CD4 molecules.
source: Further downstream, NMR has shown that the ICD of human CD4 contains a helix-turn structure, the sequence of which is highly conserved in mammalian CD4 molecules (gray shaded region, 429–442, Figure 1A, B, D; Kim et al., 2003; Willbold and Rösch, 1996).
evidence: This is based on prior NMR structural work and conservation analysis.

claim: A conserved IKRLL motif is embedded within the helix and its origins likely trace back to the predicted amniote most recent common ancestor via the presence of a dileucine repeat.
source: A conserved IKRLL motif is embedded within the helix. Its origins likely trace back to the predicted amniote most recent common ancestor (node 1) via the presence of a dileucine repeat.
evidence: This is based on phylogenetic reconstruction and represents an inference about evolutionary origins.

claim: I434, L437, and L438 are reported to regulate CD4–Lck interactions and endocytosis.
source: Many of these residues are important for the helix-turn structure, while I434, L437, and L438 are reported to regulate CD4–Lck interactions and endocytosis, suggesting that they are under purifying selection due to their role in a multifunctional hub (Kim et al., 2003; Sleckman et al., 1992).
evidence: This is reported in prior work, supported by citations.

claim: C-terminal to the CQC clasp, mammalian CD4 contains a consensus HRΦQK motif (mouse 448–452) that is not present in extant fish, reptiles, birds, or marsupial CD4 orthologs.
source: Finally, C-terminal to the CQC clasp, mammalian CD4 contains a consensus HRΦQK motif (mouse 448–452 in which Φ represents a large hydrophobic residue; Figure 1A). This putative motif is not present in extant fish, reptiles, birds, or even the marsupial CD4 orthologs sequenced to date.
evidence: This is based on phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Within the mammalian dataset, the codons for H448 and R449 were found to be under purifying selection.
source: Yet, within the mammalian dataset, the codons for H448 and R449 were found to be under purifying selection (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on the dN:dS analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Five pairs of covarying residues were identified within the ICD helix-turn region: S432–I434, S432–S439, I434–K441, L437–S439, and L437–K442.
source: By analyzing the full dataset we identified five pairs of covarying residues within the ICD helix-turn region (S432–I434; S432–S439; I434–K441; L437–S439; L437–K442), which may be relevant to the structure of this region, its function, or both (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on covariation analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: G402 covaries with L438, suggesting covariation between the TMD and ICD.
source: Interestingly, G402 covaries with L438, suggesting covariation between the TMD and ICD.
evidence: This is based on covariation analysis and represents an inference about functional relationships.

claim: H423 covaries with I434 and S439, and R426 covaries with S439.
source: Furthermore, H423 covaries with I434 and S439, and R426 covaries with S439.
evidence: This is based on covariation analysis.

claim: P228 and P281 of the nonpolar patch in the D3 domain show strong covariation with residues in the ICD helix.
source: We also found that P228 and P281 of the nonpolar patch in the D3 domain of the ECD show strong covariation with residues in the ICD helix.
evidence: This is based on covariation analysis.

claim: P228 covaried with S432, I434, S439, and K441.
source: Specifically, our data suggest that P228 covaried with S432, I434, S439, and K441
evidence: This is based on covariation analysis.

claim: P281 covaried with S432, L438, and K442.
source: while P281 covaried with S432, L438, and K442.
evidence: This is based on covariation analysis.

claim: The TP and TPC mutants were significantly reduced in DRM localization compared to WT CD4.
source: AUC analysis showed that the Palm and Clasp mutants trended lower than WT for DRM localization in our sample size, consistent with prior work (Fragoso et al., 2003), while the TP and TPC mutants were significantly reduced.
evidence: This is based on sucrose gradient fractionation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The GGXXG plus CV+C motifs together mediate CD4 localization to DRMs.
source: These data indicate that the GGXXG plus CV +C motifs together mediate CD4 localization to DRMs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional data from the TP mutant.

claim: The Clasp and TPC mutants within DRMs had reduced CTxB staining.
source: AUC analysis revealed that the Clasp and TPC mutants within DRMs had reduced CTxB staining, and the TP mutant had lower CTxB staining than the Palm mutant.
evidence: This is based on CTxB staining data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Palm, Clasp, TP, and TPC mutants all had greatly reduced Lck association in DRMs compared to WT.
source: The Palm, Clasp, TP, and TPC signals were all greatly reduced for AUC analysis of the DRM, indicating that both the CV +C and clasp motifs influence association with Lck in DRMs.
evidence: This is based on Lck co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Only the Clasp and TPC mutants had reduced Lck association in DSMs.
source: AUC analysis also showed that only the Clasp and TPC mutants had reduced Lck association in DSMs, whereas the Palm mutant trended higher, and the TP mutant had significantly increased association with Lck relative to the WT.
evidence: This is based on Lck co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A hierarchy of IL-2 production of WT > TMD > Palm > Clasp ≥ TP ≥ TPC was observed in response to a titration of MCC.
source: We observed a hierarchy of IL-2 production of WT > TMD > Palm > Clasp ≥ TP ≥ TPC in response to a titration of MCC (Figure 2D) that was reflected in AUC analysis.
evidence: This is based on IL-2 ELISA data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Only the TPC mutant impacted TCR endocytosis.
source: Of note, only the TPC mutant impacted TCR endocytosis, which is typically a measure of triggered TCRs
evidence: This is based on endocytosis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: CD4 endocytosis inversely mirrored the normalized CD4–Lck signal in DRMs.
source: while CD4 endocytosis inversely mirrored the normalized CD4–Lck signal in DRMs
evidence: This is based on comparing endocytosis and Lck association data.

claim: The CV+C and GGXXG motifs together enhance pMHCII responses by impacting CD4 membrane domain localization rather than CD4–Lck association.
source: Overall, the data suggest that the CV +C and GGXXG motifs together enhance pMHCII responses by impacting CD4 membrane domain localization rather than CD4–Lck association.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional data from multiple mutants.

claim: The TP mutant had higher overall CD4–Lck association than the WT.
source: Indeed, we found higher overall CD4–Lck association in the TP cells than the WT (Figure 2—figure supplement 4 and Supplementary file 1)
evidence: This is based on total Lck association data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The frequency of CD4–Lck pairs is not the chief determinant of IL-2 responses to agonist pMHCII in this system.
source: supporting the conclusion that the frequency of CD4–Lck pairs is not the chief determinant of IL-2 responses to agonist pMHCII in this system.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the TP mutant has more CD4-Lck pairs but reduced IL-2 responses.

claim: Both the H and HC mutants showed a higher magnitude and sensitivity of IL-2 responses to agonist pMHCII than the WT.
source: Both mutants localized in DRMs and DSMs similar to the WT, both reduced CD4–Lck interactions as expected from prior work, and yet, unexpectedly, both showed a higher magnitude and sensitivity of IL-2 responses to agonist pMHCII than the WT (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3; Kim et al., 2003; Sleckman et al., 1992).
evidence: This is based on IL-2 ELISA data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The H mutant had more TCR endocytosis than the WT or HC mutant.
source: We also observed more TCR endocytosis for the H mutant than the WT or HC mutant, indicating that the increased IL-2 output by the H mutant might reflect more triggered TCRs over the course of 16 hr.
evidence: This is based on endocytosis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The H and HC mutants failed to endocytose CD4 over the course of 16 hr of co-culture with APCs.
source: Finally, because CD4 can increase TCR dwell time on pMHCII, the failure of the H and HC mutant CD4 molecules to endocytose over the course of 16 hr of 58α−β− cell co-culture with antigen-presenting cells (APCs) could result in more sustained signaling in that time period and partially explain the increased IL-2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 4; Glassman et al., 2018; Sleckman et al., 1992).
evidence: This is based on endocytosis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The LL mutant had greatly increased IL-2 response magnitude and sensitivity to agonist pMHCII compared with the WT even though the total amount of CD4-associated Lck was lower.
source: For IL-2 we found that both the responses magnitude and sensitivity to agonist pMHCII were greatly increased for the LL mutant compared with the WT even though the total amount of CD4-associated Lck was lower (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on IL-2 ELISA and Lck association data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The SS line had higher total CD4-associated Lck than the WT yet the magnitude and sensitivity of IL-2 responses were lower.
source: In contrast, the SS line had higher total CD4-associated Lck than the WT yet the magnitude and sensitivity of IL-2 responses were lower.
evidence: This is based on IL-2 ELISA and Lck association data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: CD4–Lck interactions are not the chief determinant of IL-2 responses to agonist pMHCII in this system.
source: These data further support the idea that CD4–Lck interactions are not the chief determinant of IL-2 responses to agonist pMHCII in this system.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that mutants with different CD4-Lck levels have unexpected IL-2 responses.

claim: The IKRLL motif functions to inhibit the magnitude and sensitivity of pMHCII responses.
source: Together, the data suggest that the IKRLL motif functions to inhibit the magnitude and sensitivity of pMHCII responses and that phosphorylation of the flanking serines regulate this activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional data from the LL, SS, pSS, and LL+pSS mutants.

claim: Phosphorylation of the flanking serines regulates the inhibitory activity of the IKRLL motif.
source: Together, the data suggest that the IKRLL motif functions to inhibit the magnitude and sensitivity of pMHCII responses and that phosphorylation of the flanking serines regulate this activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional data from the SS, pSS, and LL+pSS mutants.

claim: The LL mutation lowers the signaling threshold that must be overcome for IL-2 production.
source: The simplest interpretation of these data, when considered with the increased sensitivity and response magnitude measured by ELISA, is that the LL mutation lowers the signaling threshold that must be overcome for IL-2 production.
evidence: This is an inference based on ELISpot and ELISA data.

claim: The LL + ELXE double mutant drove similar IL-2 response magnitude and sensitivity to agonist pMHCII as the WT.
source: We found that the LL + ELXE double mutant drove similar IL-2 response magnitude and sensitivity to agonist pMHCII as the WT, while the LL + Δbind double mutant completely impaired responses (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is based on IL-2 ELISA data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The intracellular helix and IKRLL motif do not regulate pMHCII-independent activity of CD4.
source: Therefore, the intracellular helix and IKRLL motif therein do not regulate pMHCII-independent activity of CD4 in our system
evidence: This is an inference based on the LL + Δbind mutant data.

claim: The intracellular helix and IKRLL motif counterbalance the formation of a stable TCR–CD3–pMHCII–CD4 assembly mediated by the ectodomain nonpolar patch.
source: rather, they counterbalance the formation of a stable TCR–CD3–pMHCII–CD4 assembly mediated by the ectodomain nonpolar patch.
evidence: This is an inference based on the LL + ELXE mutant data.

claim: Cells expressing the LL + TP double mutant had similar IL-2 responses to the WT.
source: We found that cells expressing the double mutant had similar IL-2 responses to the WT, which were lower than the LL cells only, indicating that motifs within the TMD and ectodomain can exert counterbalancing activities on pMHCII responses (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is based on IL-2 ELISA data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Motifs within the TMD and ectodomain can exert counterbalancing activities on pMHCII responses.
source: indicating that motifs within the TMD and ectodomain can exert counterbalancing activities on pMHCII responses (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the LL + TP mutant data.

claim: The Clasp mutant had reduced Zap70 and Plcγ1 phosphorylation in response to agonist pMHCII.
source: We did observe reduced Zap70 and Plcγ1 phosphorylation in response to agonist pMHCII, which helps explain the reduced IL-2 responses reported here and elsewhere for CQC clasp mutants (Glaichenhaus et al., 1991).
evidence: This is based on phosphorylation data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The TP mutant had lower CD3ζ, Zap70, and Plcγ1 phosphorylation compared to WT.
source: For the TP mutant, pCD3ζ MFI levels were significantly lower than WT for two of three independently generated cell lines tested in response to the agonist pMHCII, MCC:I-Ek, while all three TP lines had slightly higher percent responders for pCD3ζ than their paired WTs (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on phosphorylation data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: CD4–Lck pairs must be localized in the appropriate membrane compartment for efficient phosphorylation of CD3ζ when the CQC clasp is intact.
source: We therefore take these data as evidence that when the CQC clasp is intact, CD4–Lck pairs must be localized in the appropriate membrane compartment for efficient phosphorylation of CD3ζ.
evidence: This is an inference based on the TP mutant phosphorylation data.

claim: The LL mutant showed no consistent difference in pCD3ζ, pZap70, or PLCγ1 MFI or percent responders compared to WT.
source: For the LL mutant, we observed no consistent difference in pCD3ζ, pZap70, or PLCγ1 MFI or percent responders that would allow us to attribute the increase in IL-2 for the LL mutant to proximal signaling differences in response to the agonist pMHCII, MCC:I-Ek, at least not within the 2 min at which these events were evaluated (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on phosphorylation data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The interactions regulated by the intracellular helix do not consistently impact early signaling events as measured at 2 minutes.
source: These data suggest the interactions regulated by the intracellular helix, including CD4–Lck interactions, do not consistently impact early signaling events as measured here.
evidence: This is an inference based on the LL mutant phosphorylation data.

claim: The Clasp mutant did not show consistent differences in pCD3ζ MFI levels in response to the weak agonist T102S:I-Ek.
source: Two of the lines showed no difference in pCD3ζ MFI levels between the Clasp mutant and paired WT, another had a pCD3ζ MFI for the Clasp mutant that was ~117% of the WT, and the last line had pCD3ζ MFI for the Clasp mutant that was ~80% of WT.
evidence: This is based on phosphorylation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The IL-2 responses to APCs expressing the tethered T102S:I-Ek were lower for the Clasp mutants in all four sets of lines relative to their paired WT controls.
source: Importantly, the IL-2 responses to APCs expressing the tethered T102S:I-Ek were lower for the Clasp mutants in all four sets of lines relative to their paired WT controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is based on IL-2 data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: The phosphorylation states of the helix serines regulate the functions of the IKRLL motif.
source: Our SS, pSS, and LL + pSS mutants all suggest that the phosphorylation states of the helix serines regulates these functions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional data from the SS, pSS, and LL+pSS mutants.

claim: The multifunctional intracellular helix is a key regulator of pMHCII responses.
source: We take these data as evidence that the multifunctional intracellular helix is a key regulator of pMHCII responses.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional data from multiple helix mutants.

claim: The emergence of the CD4 intracellular helix with its ability to counterbalance the signal-enhancing activity of other motifs was a key moment in the regulation of mammalian CD4 function.
source: The broader conclusion from these results is that the emergence of the CD4 intracellular helix, with its ability to counterbalance the signal-enhancing activity of other motifs, was a key moment in the regulation of mammalian CD4 function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the evolutionary and functional data.
